lines.trans: Yeah, that is me—I am Producer T! I am totally fine.
Are you all right? People have been talking nonstop since the morning article broke, and I heard someone vandalized your car…
It is fine—baseless rumors like this get talked up and then die back down once people realize they are false.
What are all these texts suddenly—I am getting cursed out for a lifetime! CEO Byun really knows how to work the media.
How could they have found your phone number? Ah—the contact number posted inside your windshield!
Oh my goodness, did they really get it by looking at that?
Take that card off first, and please stay careful for a while—you never know who might jump out to harm you.
Wait—that motorcycle looks suspicious too!
I nearly got hurt worse right now because of you! Honestly, you are way too dramatic!

examples.text: 응, 근데 너 왜 갑자기 선배라고 해? 님 자 어디 갔어?
examples.trans: Yeah, wait—why are you suddenly calling me plain Senior? Where did the honorific suffix go?

examples.text: 뭐야, 왜 대답을 못 해? 갑자기 왜 선배님이 선배가 됐지?
examples.trans: What is it, why can you not answer? How did honored Senior suddenly turn into plain Senior?

meanings.note: Used in -(으)ㄴ/는 것 같다 to express 'it seems that...' or 'I think...'.

meanings.en: to be the same, to be like

examples.trans: I think I'm late.
It looks like it's going to rain.

meanings.note: Bound noun often contracted to 거 in everyday speech.

examples.trans: This is my bag.
Because I think I'm late.

meanings.note: Honorific equivalent of 있다; used in 안녕히 계세요 ('goodbye' to someone staying).

examples.trans: Goodbye! (to someone staying)
Is the teacher inside right now?

괜찮다.gloss: to be fine; to be okay

meanings.en: to be fine; to be okay; to be alright
meanings.note: Used to reassure someone, decline an offer politely, or say something is acceptable.

examples.trans: I'm really fine.
Is it okay if we meet tomorrow?
Where did you buy that?
That is a really good idea.
dummy trans 1
dummy trans 2

meanings.note: written piece in a newspaper or online media

examples.trans: I read that article this morning.

examples.text: 새 드라마에 대한 기사가 많이 나왔어요.
examples.trans: Many articles came out about the new drama.

meanings.note: Plain first-person singular pronoun used with friends, younger people, or subordinates; contracts to 난 with -는 and becomes 내가 before -가.

examples.trans: I'm going to stay home today.
I'll go first.

meanings.en: to arise, to come up, to occur
meanings.note: Used with feelings, thoughts, or events (e.g. 실감이 나다, 생각이 나다).

examples.trans: A good idea came to mind.
Tears suddenly came to my eyes.
Do you have time today?
Where are you going?

meanings.note: Used only with close friends, younger people, or children
interrogative pronoun; becomes 누가 before subject particle -가

examples.trans: Did someone come outside?
Who is that person?

다치다.gloss: to get hurt, to be injured

examples.trans: I fell and hurt my knee.
Be careful not to get hurt.

examples.text: 내가 당분간 너 술 먹지 말라 그랬지, 입 조심해야 된다고!
examples.trans: I told you not to drink for the time being because you have to watch your mouth!
Here the word for 'for the time being' is key.
He is our company's president.
I will speak as the representative.

meanings.note: Takes a complement marked with 이/가.

examples.trans: I want to become a doctor.
It has already become 12 o'clock.

meanings.note: Usually followed by -e to mean 'because of'.

examples.trans: I was late because of the rain.
It's because of you.

examples.text: 괜찮아, 이런 헛소문 어차피 떠들다가 아니다 싶으면 또 사그라드는 거야.
examples.trans: It is fine—baseless rumors like this get talked up and then die back down once people realize they are false.
Let us do that (chattering away, then) right away.

examples.text: 일단 그거 떼시고요, 당분간 조심하셔야 될 것 같습니다. 어디서 누가 튀어나와서 해코지할지 모르니까.
examples.trans: Take that card off first, and please stay careful for a while—you never know who might jump out to harm you.

examples.text: 일단 그거 떼시고요, 당분간 조심하셔야 될 것 같습니다.
examples.trans: Take that card down first, and please stay cautious for the time being.
See you again!
It is raining again.

meanings.en: to be many, numerous, or abundant
meanings.note: Used for both countable and uncountable nouns.

examples.trans: Because it's the weekend, there are many people at the department store.

examples.text: 오늘 해야 할 일이 너무 많다.
examples.trans: There is too much work to do today.

meanings.note: Combines with 하다 in 말하다 (to speak, to say).

examples.trans: I don't know what you mean.
You speak Korean well.

meanings.note: Everyday verb for eating a meal or food; honorific equivalent is 드시다.

examples.trans: Let's eat lunch together.
Did you eat breakfast?

meanings.en: to not know, to be unaware of
meanings.note: 르-irregular verb: stem 모르- + -아요/-았어요 → 몰라요 / 몰랐어요.

examples.trans: I don't know well either.
I didn't realize time was passing.

meanings.note: colloquial contraction of 무엇; also used rhetorically to brush off a question

examples.trans: What are you doing now?
Why are you even asking something like that?

보다.gloss: to see, to watch; to take (an exam)

meanings.en: to see, to look at, to watch

examples.trans: I watched a movie on the weekend.
I took the driver's license exam.

examples.text: 전화번호 어떻게 알았을까요? 아, 차 창문 앞에 붙여놓은 전화번호!
examples.trans: How could they have found your phone number? Ah—the contact number posted inside your windshield!

examples.text: 어떻게 알았을까요? 창문 앞에 붙여놓은 전화번호!
examples.trans: How could they have known? The phone number stuck inside the windshield!

examples.text: 가란다고 갔으면 나 진짜로 외로워질 뻔했어.
examples.trans: If you had actually left just because I told you to, I would have gotten truly lonely.

examples.text: 나 너 때문에 더 다칠 뻔했잖아 지금! 아무튼 너 유난스럽다 진짜!
examples.trans: I nearly got hurt worse right now because of you! Honestly, you are way too dramatic!

examples.text: 괜찮아, 이런 헛소문 어차피 떠들다가 아니다 싶으면 또 사그라드는 거야.

examples.text: 아니요 저는 아무도 아닙니다, 대화 편하게 나누세요. 저는 진짜 수상한 사람인 줄 알고…
examples.trans: Oh no, I am nobody special—please chat comfortably. I genuinely thought he was a suspicious person…

meanings.note: Auxiliary adjective attached to a verb stem with -고 (-고 싶다).

examples.trans: I want to go to Korea.
I want to drink a cup of coffee.

meanings.note: Expresses sudden realization, surprise, or hesitation.

examples.trans: Ah, yes.
Oh, I see!

meanings.note: Negative copula used with nouns (often with -이/가)

examples.trans: It is not my fault.
Today is not Sunday, it's Monday.

examples.text: 아무튼 걱정하지 마십시오. 주소 공유 관계는 발설하지 않겠습니다.
examples.trans: Anyway, please do not worry. I will not breathe a word about the address-sharing arrangement.

examples.text: 아무튼 저 촬영장에서도 피디님만 보고 가요. 수고하세요.
examples.trans: Anyway, I am going to the set counting only on you. Keep up the good work.

examples.text: 변 대표랑 준모랑 서로 쌍소리 오가고 촬영장 아주 개판 됐대요.
examples.trans: They say CEO Byun and Joon-mo traded harsh words and the set turned into a total mess.

I woke up early in the morning.
Did you eat breakfast?

meanings.note: Used in standard farewells 안녕히 계세요 and 안녕히 가세요.

examples.trans: Goodbye! (to someone staying)
Goodbye! (to someone leaving)

meanings.note: ㄹ-irregular verb: stem 알- drops ㄹ before ㄴ, ㅂ, ㅅ (e.g., 압니까)

examples.trans: Do you know that person's phone number?
Yes, I know well.
Go forward.
Do well in the future.
Where is the restroom?
Where are you right now?
How did you get here?
How should we solve this problem?
Oh my, so nice to meet you!
Oh my, I left my phone behind.
Stop, that is enough—it was all a lie anyway!
Here the word for 'anyway, in any case' is key.

examples.text: 나 걱정 안 해요, 대표님이 알아서 언론플레이 다 해주니까.
examples.trans: I am not worried, since you handle all the media play on your own, CEO.

examples.text: 뭐야 갑자기, 욕을 아주 원 없이 먹는구나! 변 대표가 진짜 언론플레이 제대로 한다.
examples.trans: What are all these texts suddenly—I am getting cursed out for a lifetime! CEO Byun really knows how to work the media.

없다.gloss: to not exist, to not have

meanings.en: to not exist, to not be present

examples.trans: I only have a thousand won.
That is ten thousand won in total.

examples.trans: I nearly got hurt worse right now because of you! Honestly, you are way too dramatic!

meanings.en: first of all, for starters, for the time being
meanings.note: marks an immediate first step before dealing with anything else

examples.trans: Let's sit down and talk first.
Let's wait until today for now.

meanings.note: Humble first-person singular pronoun used in polite speech.

examples.trans: I have an induction ceremony.
Follow me.
What is your phone number?
I changed my phone number.
I understand well (properly).
Today is a (properly) busy day.

meanings.note: Used to warn or advise caution.

examples.trans: Please be careful.
Please be careful. (2)
What time is it now?
I'll leave right now.

meanings.note: Everyday spoken intensifier; can also function as a noun meaning 'the real thing'.

examples.trans: I'm really busy today.
Is that really delicious?
This is my father's car.
I parked the car in the parking lot.

examples.text: 여긴 창문도 없다고, 감방에 독방 같잖아?
examples.trans: There are no windows in here—does it not look just like solitary confinement?
Here the word for 'even windows' is key.

examples.text: 일단 그거 떼시고요, 당분간 조심하셔야 될 것 같습니다. 어디서 누가 튀어나와서 해코지할지 모르니까.
examples.trans: Take that card off first, and please stay careful for a while—you never know who might jump out to harm you.
Let us do that (jumping out and) right away.

examples.text: 아, 마지막에 이거 넣으라고, 한편 신디는 얼마 전 특집쇼 녹화 중 담당 여자 피디인 티모 피디의 실수로 부상을 입어 입원을 한 바 있다.
examples.trans: Oh, and put this at the end: Meanwhile, Cindy was recently hospitalized after being injured during a special taping due to a mistake by female producer T.

examples.text: 공중파 방송 3사 음악 피디 중에 티모 피디가 몇이나 될까? 나 혼자겠지?
examples.trans: Among music producers at the three major networks, how many T-PDs could there be—just me, right?

examples.text: 괜찮으십니까? 아침에 기사 나고 나서 말들이 많아서요, 차도 누가 파손했다고…
examples.trans: Are you all right? People have been talking nonstop since the morning article broke, and I heard someone vandalized your car…
Let us do that (vandalized, they said…) right away.

meanings.note: Hangul spelling of the English abbreviation PD, widely used in Korean broadcasting.

examples.trans: Who is the PD in charge of the new program?

examples.text: 그녀는 예능 피디가 되기 위해 시험을 준비했다.
examples.trans: She prepared for the exam to become a variety PD.

meanings.en: to do, to perform, to hold
meanings.note: Core verb; also combines with nouns to form verbs.

examples.trans: What are you doing right now?
We are holding a meeting today.

examples.text: 일단 그거 떼시고요, 당분간 조심하셔야 될 것 같습니다. 어디서 누가 튀어나와서 해코지할지 모르니까.
examples.trans: Take that card off first, and please stay careful for a while—you never know who might jump out to harm you.
Let us do that (might harm you) right away.

examples.text: 괜찮아, 이런 헛소문 어차피 떠들다가 아니다 싶으면 또 사그라드는 거야.
examples.trans: It is fine—baseless rumors like this get talked up and then die back down once people realize they are false.
